#+title: Live rendering — progressive answers, construction-paced reveal
#+STATUS: draft
#+FIRMNESS: draft
#+FILETAGS: :turtle:render:contract:experimental:

* Charge and evidence discipline
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-contract
:LENS: empiricist adversarial systems educator
:END:

The learner should see useful work toward the current question, without a
frozen browser, an unmarked stale answer, or machine speed changing the
computation. This is a target contract, not a description of shipped behavior.
The author's rulings below choose the experience; experiments choose the
smallest machinery that can honestly deliver it. No runtime policy is changed
by this document. No experimental treatment is a decision merely because it is
listed here.

The experimental discipline is simple: keep a control, vary a named cause,
write the prediction before running, retain the inconvenient observations,
and repeat before generalizing. A fake clock establishes ordering and state
transitions, not human latency. A model sink establishes transport and model
cost, not GPU performance. A browser trace establishes one observed device,
not every display. Timings never excuse a semantic violation.

Priors to appreciate, not blindly inherit:
- D011: causal logical time; wall time reveals, never chooses event ordering.
- [[id:output-ledger-r2-credit]]: credit may delay lossless output, not erase it.
- [[id:output-ledger-r2-instant]]: a parked instant must not leak to a reader.
- [[id:output-ledger-r2-pacer]]: cooperative slices protect responsiveness;
  unpaced and paced drivers must preserve meaning.
- D055: display ownership includes geometry and identifying presentation;
  current-state slots are not deposited-ink queues.
- [[id:render-construction-cadence]]: the circle exposed work-dependent prefixes;
  its wait regression showed that whole-program completion is not readiness.
- [[id:runtime-intention-performance]]: answer age matters alongside frame gaps;
  construction, materialization, and page scheduling require separate attribution.


* Author's rulings and deliberately open choices
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-rulings
:LENS: educator adversarial
:END:

| Choice | Ruling | Cost consciously accepted |
|--------+--------+---------------------------|
| Incomplete answer | Show completed ordered progress | Visible answer can be unfinished |
| Progress granularity | Prefer macro chunks, fall back to drawable operations | Macro completeness is a preference, not an indefinite veto |
| Replacement | Mark old display; switch at first new prefix | Brief explicitly stale display |
| Supersession | Newest replacement wins, cooperative cancellation | Some intermediate questions never get an answer |
| Semantic reads | Display checkpoints create no publication boundary | Ink can be visible while a dependency is not ready |
| Overload | Slow reveal, no catch-up debt | Authored wall-time tempo is not guaranteed |
| Clock scope | One reveal horizon per play | Heavy work can slow companions |
| Replay | Defer to future recorder feature set | Same-code rerun is not promised cached-speed playback |

Open choices, not silently settled by this table:
- The authoritative reason/progress fact that gates reveal advancement.
- Existing ownership's precise replacement-region boundary.
- Drawable atomicity for fills, text, paths, placement, and asynchronous geometry.
- Bounded buffering and which layer stops consuming when downstream is full.
- Empty answers and failures before/after the first-prefix transition.
- Feedback representation and measured thresholds for fallback and pacing.

* Vocabulary — authorities must not trade places
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-vocabulary
:MODULE: assets/js/turtling/scheduler.js assets/js/turtling/compositor.js assets/js/turtling/timeline.js
:LENS: systems
:END:

- *Question*: the captured inputs that define a replaceable answer. Source text
  alone is not its identity. Code, seed, captured arguments, relevant definition
  epochs and causal inputs must be considered at their existing ownership seams.
- *Run*: one incarnation of computing that question. Existing identity and
  =runIncarnation= are candidates, not a license to invent a parallel identity store.
- *Region*: the display owned by a replacement, including owned descendants and
  related presentation. A referenced external figure need not be owned by it.
- *Logical instant*: the language's causal unit. Existing waits, yields, spawn
  rules, readiness and observation baselines govern it.
- *Drawable operation*: the smallest coherent presentation transaction we can
  apply. It may span several low-level records. A ring-buffer event is only a
  candidate; parsing syntax or a single GPU draw is not proof of atomicity.
- *Macro chunk*: a finite drawing step meaningful in the author's structure:
  one loop iteration, a recursive step before recurrence, or an owned finite
  construction. The lifetime of a recursive invocation is not necessarily finite.
  An =as= scope or =let= token alone does not prove a display boundary.
- *Prefix*: completed output in the existing canonical order for a run/region.
  It is not a cheapest-first selection. Persistent ink is ordered and lossless;
  existing current-state slots may conflate by identity. Do not impose an ink
  history discipline on those slots, or quietly conflate deposited ink.
- *Reveal horizon H*: the shared logical time currently authorized for a play.
  =tick(H)= uses it as eligibility, not as causal event order.
- *Work clock W*: monotonic elapsed time for slices, cancellation latency and
  existing residency deadlines. It continues while H is paused.
- *Opportunity*: a callback in which work or presentation may be attempted.
  rAF grants a paint opportunity; it does not grant a new logical ordering.
- *Display publication*: making output visible. This is NOT the scheduler/law
  pipeline's semantic publication or accepted motion commit.

* Target contract — observable promises
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-promises
:LENS: educator adversarial
:END:

** C01 — Causality is invariant under work and paint schedules
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-causality
:END:

For a fixed program, seed, captured question and causal input trace, with
equivalent declared admission outcomes and within the same truth/resource envelope,
changing work allowance, channel capacity or opportunity schedule must not change
accepted geometry, logical event order, or program-semantic errors. Display histories
may differ in how many completed operations they reveal at each paint.

Explicit existing resource/residency faults and host lifecycle actions are separate
outcomes, not silently excluded successes. Record them and compare the valid logical
prefix where possible. This contract does not abolish existing wall-clock residency
deadlines or promise that arbitrary resource pressure produces identical completion.

Changing =wait= changes the experiment, not just its presentation. Adding a
macro-display checkpoint must NOT inject a language yield, advance =resumeAt=,
alter an observation baseline, or make a dependency readable. No wall-time
prefix is a source of semantic state for a sibling. Existing read/commit rules
remain authoritative even when the screen reveals unfinished construction.

Replacement coalescing is a separate input policy: runs may be skipped.
Do not demand identical abandoned-run traces under different input delivery
schedules. Compare fixed questions for determinism, and for supersession compare
the eventual newest answer under the same accepted causal inputs. Never coalesce
an authored message/ink history simply because hand questions are replaceable.

** C02 — Execution may stop independently of presentation
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-execution
:END:

At work-allowance expiry or a newer replacement request, return control at a
safe cooperative checkpoint. Safety preserves existing instant ownership and
owed output; it does not require a whole figure or macro to have finished.
A finite measured extension may be investigated, but correctness must not
require finishing an arbitrarily expensive instant. A tick-count cap is not
an elapsed-time bound.

The allowance is soft. Record indivisible calls, construction setup outside
slices, readout draining, materialization and rendering. Do not claim a hard
4 ms latency merely because =withSlice(4, ...)= was requested. No input-pending
API is required for correctness; it may advise the driver as an optional hint.
A missing hint is not permission to monopolize the browser.

** C03 — Prefer meaningful chunks; never indefinitely withhold drawable progress
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-prefix
:END:

Present as much available completed ordered output from the current run as the
presentation allowance permits. Prefer finished macro chunks when they are
ready cheaply. If awaiting a chunk delays feedback, expose its completed
drawable-operation prefix. Do not wait for an endless recursive call to return.

Do not skip an expensive earlier operation merely to fit later cheap output.
If an indivisible drawable operation is expensive, that is an atomicity/design
question: measure it before adding a split. Never publish half-updated
coordinates, a torn fill, or new geometry seated using unrelated placement.
Fallback thresholds are empirical policy, not logical time and not a hidden
instruction-count budget. A macro marker is display metadata only.

Visible incompleteness must be distinguishable from completion. A progress
count may say what happened; it must not invent a percentage without a total.
No guarantee is made that every macro gets its own paint.

** C04 — Replace a region at its first coherent new prefix
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-replacement
:END:

On accepting a replacement question, make its rebuilding/awaiting-replacement
status observable at the next available UI opportunity. "Immediate" means no
intentional wait for computation; it does not promise a callback while JS is
blocked. Retain the most recently displayed region, which may itself be partial,
and identify it as not the current answer.

When the new run has an eligible prefix, retire the prior region's display and
install that prefix in one coherent presentation transition. Geometry, placement,
owned child layers, heads, labels, names, vectors, overlays and interaction
identity must be audited. No ordinary old/new overlay is allowed within one
region. Independent regions legitimately have different run identities.

Retaining a display does not resurrect its semantic bindings. A stale displayed
object must not silently accept a gesture against a retired binding. Whether
such a gesture is disabled or converted to a new current question remains an
explicit interaction choice to probe.

Empty replacement and failure behavior is open in [[id:live-rendering-edge-rulings]].
An old image must not remain indefinitely merely because a valid answer has no ink.

** C05 — Newest replacement wins through cooperative cancellation
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-cancellation
:END:

Keep the newest pending replacement per existing replaceable owner. At the next
safe checkpoint retire superseded computation and private output. Starting every
intermediate request is not required. Already-accepted causal effects are not
rolled back or re-fired merely to tidy the screen.

Every delayed admission result, readout walk, text/geometry completion, scheduled
drain and pending output must pass lifetime/run checks before affecting a new
run's display or semantic state. Cancellation must release owned staging and
accounting without losing output still owed by a surviving run. Existing
protocol gates remain; cancellation is not bypassing admission or laws.

Continuous input may starve first-prefix publication if each current question is
too expensive to reach a drawable operation. Report that condition. Activity
feedback is not evidence that answers are moving. Do not hide starvation by
publishing a superseded answer or claiming "responsive" from FPS alone.

** C06 — Construction paces one shared reveal horizon per play
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-reveal
:MODULE: assets/js/turtling/timeline.js assets/js/turtling/compositor.js
:END:

H is nondecreasing within a play, except an explicit new-play/seek action under
its existing contract. Logical birth, =resumeAt= and authored elapsed time are
not rewritten when presentation pauses. W remains monotonic and advances normally.
There is no independent reveal history for each figure in this iteration.

When eligible construction is unfinished, retain H while subsequent opportunities
continue work and reveal completed output. When the horizon is ready to advance,
resume from H rather than adding the wall time spent paused. Healthy authored
sleeping must allow H to advance toward the next logical event. Progressive ink
may appear while H stays fixed.

Illustration, not an implementation algorithm: if H=0 needs several work
opportunities to construct, its later =wait 0.1= is not made overdue by those
construction delays. Once eligible work closes and reveal resumes, the remaining
logical distance is still respected. Display time is not a hard real-time promise.

The precise "unfinished" and "ready to advance" facts are the central open
experiment. Do NOT freeze because =!done=, =worldProgress.phase === 'building'=
or a future =resumeAt= exists. Do NOT advance merely because one body ended,
one tick returned false, or =atCut= was true once. Treat dataflow/admission/credit
pressure, done owners with living descendants and zero-time recurrence explicitly.

Ordinary foreground congestion, hidden-tab suspension, render-on-demand idle,
new play, edit, seek and batch invocation are distinct causes. Do not use a noisy
rAF gap alone to decide which occurred. Existing idle-rebase behavior must be
regression-tested before changing it. Batch/flush need not acquire live timing
policy merely to share transport and logical semantics.

** C07 — Bounded transport is not output loss
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-bounds
:END:

Drain channels to return credit, even when a preferred macro boundary is not yet
ready. Draining is not semantic publication and need not immediately present.
If draining moves data into staging, the staging has a declared bound and an
accounted owner. A full downstream stage must eventually backpressure upstream,
not create an unbounded alternate ledger. Preserve owed-event retry and canonical
ordering. Current-state slots keep their existing conflation discipline.

Count retained old geometry, current geometry, pending output, upload buffers,
labels and cancellation remnants. Existing segment counters are not a complete
byte-residency measurement. Do not erase the old display merely because its
semantic frame left the registry before replacement is ready.

Classify every new bound as rate or truth. Rate delays/retries; truth faults
honestly under the existing admission/residency policy. No silently dropped ink,
new truth ceiling, or revised residency policy is earned by this document.

** C08 — Measure scheduling roles separately
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-pacing
:MODULE: assets/js/turtling/pacer.js assets/js/turtling/render/loop.js
:END:

Paint opportunity, work allowance and stopped/hidden detection are separate
responsibilities. Instrument pump, setup/readout, drain/materialize, scene update
and render submission before changing the pacer. Callback gaps are evidence of
delivery, not an attribution of work cost or proof of display refresh rate.

Pump-only feedback is also insufficient when materialization or other page work
dominates. Separate observations from the control policy. A known allowance
consumed by a pump is not independent evidence of spare capacity. Variable-refresh,
missed callbacks, external load and idle gaps need controls.

No worker, idle speculation beyond H, alternative frame source, per-figure
priority, reduced-motion execution rule, or browser-specific input API is required
by this first contract. If evidence justifies one later, give it only the authority
it needs. Reduced motion is a presentation concern, not inherently a slice rule.

** C09 — Deferred replay stays deferred
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-replay-deferred
:END:

First run and rerun are live computation with construction-paced reveal. An
explicit rerun must follow the existing new-play semantics; unchanged source is
not permission to promise a stored timeline. A future recorder may separately
specify result identity, logical output timestamps, effects, retained history,
partial/endless playback, and render-cache invalidation. Do not replay computational
messages or admission effects as a shortcut to repeating an animation.

* Edge rulings to earn, not bury
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-edge-rulings
:LENS: adversarial
:END:

| Edge | Candidate default to test | What would force another ruling |
|------+---------------------------+---------------------------------|
| Valid empty answer | Retire old display at an explicit eligible empty result | Empty mistaken for blocked/no-output-yet |
| Failure before first new prefix | Keep prior display, mark failed and stale | Old result presented as valid for new question |
| Failure after first new prefix | Keep new partial display marked failed; no silent resurrection | Learner cannot distinguish incomplete/error state |
| Permanent dependency block | Keep feedback truthful; UI alive; no busy retry spin | Clock pause hides an actionable unresolved state |
| Async admission | Honor instant ownership; no future leak; expose waiting cause | Delayed reply can publish into retired run |
| Zero-time endless recurrence | Responsive progressive output; diagnose horizon progress explicitly | Global freeze/starvation classified as healthy sleeping |
| Interaction with stale geometry | Disable retired target or explicitly rebind as a new question | Hit-test routes into dead owner or misleading position |
| Async text/geometry | Treat coherently completed visual unit as eligible | Ink/name appears after cancellation or against wrong placement |

These are recommendations, not additional author-approved decisions. Bring the
observations back before fixing them as contract.

* Baseline — what stands and what does not
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-baseline
:LENS: empiricist
:END:

The initial focused run passed 24 tests in compositor_budget, figure_cadence and
scheduler_determinism. The later extended regression floor passed 69; two final P0
process runs produced identical records. [[id:live-rendering-results]] holds exact
provenance, the inconvenient pilot, and limits. This is not target-contract coverage.
Current behavior differs from the target:
- =advance(t)= supplies =t - epoch=; normal construction does not pause H.
- =withSlice= supplies cooperative execution time, not reveal-clock accounting.
- =driveToRest= crosses expiry while =!atCut=, capped by 64 overrun ticks;
  the cap is neither a time bound nor proof of closure. It then materializes.
- Channels and current-state slots materialize directly; no owner-keyed collector
  file exists in this checkout although earlier specs describe one.
- The current restart test expects new ink before recipe completion. It does not
  establish marked staleness or an atomic first-prefix region transition.
- =hotSwapChild= pumps via =advanceChild=; it does not call =driveToRest=.
  =captureFrame= samples the canvas; it does not itself drive logical work.
- =worldProgress= calls living waited frames "building"; that reader is feedback,
  not yet an authoritative pause signal.
- P0 found =atCut=true= with an open, breath-suspended descendant under ended
  ancestors: its traversal skips done intermediate bodies. Preserve this witness
  before using the reader as an authoritative horizon gate.
- P1 reference/state panel and five driver-model H pairs ran twice with identical
  records. Finite/prefix canonical comparisons agree; healthy waits and no-debt
  predictions hold in this model. Promotion is rejected: blind admission retry
  lacks a wake, and reference scanning is not an authoritative stop summary.
- Traversal repair alone is insufficient: both cut readers can be true with a
  queued derived move, or a closed due body before its next tick. Missing names
  may wound rather than remain blocked; no-time recursion hit a host stack fault.
  [[id:live-rendering-p1-results]] retains these contrary readings and pilot repairs.
- The full existing JS floor now reports 2756 pass, 0 fail, 1 existing TODO across
  206 files. P2–P7 candidate treatments are still not run; gate ambiguity stops
  integration under the stopping rule below. No runtime policy changed.

Preserve baseline tests. If a target intentionally changes one, retain the old
witness and record why its expectation changes; do not turn evidence green by
removing the counterexample. Historical collector/performance findings remain
priors, not proof of a module currently wired here.

* Observations — collect answers, not just frames
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-observation-schema
:LENS: empiricist
:END:

For each input/work/presentation record, capture only available fields and label
unknowns. Do not infer an exact stop reason from a boolean progress return.

| Axis | Required observations |
|------+-----------------------|
| Provenance | HEADs, relevant dirty-source digest, fixture hash, runtime/browser/device, configuration, treatment, seed, schedule |
| Identity | owner/region, accepted question revision, active run, displayed run, queued newest request |
| Time | wall opportunity timestamp, monotonic work span, H before/after, logical frontier, elapsed/resumeAt/birth |
| Work | setup/readouts, pump, drain/materialize, positions/cleanup, render submission, longest unbroken call, slice requested/actual |
| State | midInstant, suspension kind, body done, owned descendant state, tick progress, building, atCut, next due event if known |
| Transport | event/point/byte counts, channel/staging/slot high-water, owed event, returned credit, disposal and retained bytes |
| Experience | acknowledgement latency, first-new-prefix latency, displayed answer age, longest unchanged-prefix interval, completion latency |
| Cancellation | request-to-checkpoint latency, obsolete work cost, rejected late completions, surviving stale mutations |
| Outcome | canonical output/accepted-geometry trace, semantic errors, presentation transitions, pause/resume reasons |

CPU render submission is not GPU completion. Heap is not GPU residency. A schema
field is not a claim that an instrument can measure it yet. Measure instrumentation
on/off overhead; avoid full-tree snapshots in every production frame.

* Experiments — hypotheses and falsifiers before treatments
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-experiments
:LENS: empiricist adversarial
:END:

** P0 — Diagnostic baseline: are execution and reveal already coupled?
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p0
:END:

Instrument: [[file:../../probe/live-rendering/diagnose.mjs][diagnose.mjs]]. Real scheduler/parser and headless real compositor;
identity admission supplies declared synthetic work cost. No runtime treatment.

Prediction: a cooperative parked construction can coexist with an advancing
=t - epoch= horizon; a healthy waited frame can report feedback "building"
without an unfinished instant. Credit/admission/no-progress must not be collapsed
into one boolean. Materialized prefix size need not equal logical readiness.

Controls: fixed seed/question, explicit clock/capacity/breath settings, future
wait sampled before and at its due time, root and descendant state both recorded.
Falsifier: construction already suppresses H, or existing status fully separates
these cases. Reuse that mechanism rather than add one. The synthetic work clock
is not milliseconds of device performance; no input-latency conclusion follows.

** P1 — State classification and horizon gate spike
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p1
:END:

Experiment concluded: [[id:live-rendering-p1-results]] and [[id:live-rendering-stopwake-results]].
Repeated model/state trials and corrected stop/wake isolation reject live promotion.
[[id:live-rendering-learnings]] records the next work: owner-specific eligibility facts,
not another clock heuristic. Unrun residency and driver-lifecycle witnesses remain open.

Question: can existing suspension/instant/ownership facts supply a small honest
stop summary without a second dirty graph or repeated whole-tree scan?

Fixtures: authored future wait; finite CPU-breathed macro; full channel; pending
admission; missing-yet-spawnable dependency; dependency cycle; ended owner with
waiting child; nested recurrence with/without wait; zero-time infinite recurrence;
permanent block; failure; explicit done; queued derived move after cached done.

Compare candidate existing =building=, =atCut=, tick return, due-frontier and
suspension combinations against the actual next legal transition. Record ambiguity,
not just whether a getter is convenient. Any loop safety ceiling belongs to the
instrument, is reported as censored, and never becomes a runtime truth bound.

Spike: driver-only shared-H accumulator with stop causes derived from existing
facts. Keep logical =resumeAt=, birth and ordering unchanged. Compare only horizon
policy, with identical fixed work budget and presentation sink.

Predictions: ordinary waiting advances H; unfinished eligible work retains it;
paused W still advances; resumed H gets no paused-wall delta; done parents do
not erase child pressure. A no-time endless process must not hang the browser.
Falsifiers: wait deadlock, causal trace change, undisclosed catch-up burst, busy
retry without wake, or O(frames × pending-regions) classification cost.

** P2 — Drawable atomicity and macro usefulness spike
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p2
:END:

Use the same final geometry written as straight-line commands, loop iterations,
finite helper calls and recursive steps, preserving causal timing. Separately test
as/let descendants, long paths, turn-only sequences, fill, colour/thickness changes,
clear, labels, declared vectors, camera/target-frame placement and delayed text.
Equivalent syntax fixtures must first prove equivalence; adding waits is not a
valid same-geometry control for a coupled program.

Treatment: presentation-only macro metadata plus bounded fallback. Control:
completed drawable operations without preferred grouping. Strict macro-only
presentation is a negative control for a very large iteration, not a recommended
replacement for the author's choice. Keep execution and clocks fixed.

Prediction: small chunks give intelligible progress; expensive chunks still expose
coherent prefixes; no new logical yield/readiness boundary appears. Compare first
ink, completion, presentation overhead and operation coherency. Falsifiers: a
recursive result waits forever, metadata changes computation, marker retention
leaks, or a nominal drawable needs atomic placement/state not captured by its event.

** P3 — Region ownership, replacement and cancellation spike
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p3
:END:

Drive questions A/B/C into the same existing slot during setup, halfway through a
macro, after first prefix, while waiting, during admission, before async geometry
completion and immediately before disposal. Deliver old replies in reversed order.
Include rename, same-key control, true new play, reset/withdrawal, nested children,
ink deposited into another layer, shared material reuse and external references.

Control: a fixed question with no supersession and an unrelated independent region.
Compare input coalescing separately from cancellation/presentation lifetime; do not
conflate their savings. Record displayed/active identities on each presentation,
not just last-frame geometry. Final settled newest answer must equal its isolated
execution for the same captured causal inputs.

Prediction: acknowledgement does not wait for construction; old display persists
marked; first prefix retires the owned old region coherently; cancelled asynchronous
work neither mutates nor resurrects it. Falsifiers: mixed ink/placement/name, stale
hit-target, obsolete reply accepted, unaccounted retained child, or starvation
masked by stable FPS. Test empty/failed answers explicitly before ruling on them.

** P4 — Credit and memory conservation spike
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p4
:END:

Run the same surviving question at channel capacities 1, 2, 16 and 512; alternate
small/large output, small presentation allowance, a large macro and delayed sink.
Compare drains during construction with ordinary live draining. Test cancelling
while an event is owed and while old/new geometry coexist.

Prediction: equal canonical surviving ink/geometry at all capacities; no duplicate
owed event; returned credit permits completion without presenting a preferred
macro prematurely; staging and retained resources have bounded accounted owners.
Falsifiers: deadlock, lost/reordered persistent ink, unbounded staging, mutation of
closed old channels into new display, or residency policy altered without a ruling.
Declared vectors/heads must retain slot semantics rather than wait behind ink.

Separate cumulative valid ink growth from leaked replacement resources. For an
endless drawing, total memory cannot plateau unless existing truth policy faults
or output is explicitly withdrawn; "bounded queues" is not "bounded total art".

** P5 — Controlled cost attribution and pacer comparison
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p5
:END:

First collect browser spans under four loads: expensive computation/cheap display;
cheap computation/expensive materialization; external page work with cheap drawing;
and normal idle/hidden/resume behavior. Test requested/delivered cadences near
30/60/120 Hz and missed-callback schedules; emulation is not a physical refresh test.

Only after attribution compare fixed budget, current interval feedback, pump-only
feedback as a negative control, and an evidence-based multi-span policy. Do not
change cadence estimator and allowance controller in the same first comparison.

Prediction: interval-only cannot attribute external load; pump-only can overbid
when display dominates; missed callbacks must not teach the estimator that overload
is a slower healthy panel. Falsifiers: controller ratchets under healthy delivery,
starves progress, improves FPS while worsening first-prefix age, or introduces an
unbounded synchronous setup/materialization span outside its measured budget.

** P6 — Browser experience and ensemble slowdown
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p6
:END:

Real pointer/edit sequences: isolated changes, bursts, sustained dragging, pause
then final input, and background/resume. Heavy figure plus lightweight dependent
and independent companions; authored waits short/long/incommensurate. Use the
learner's circle and blue variant, not only synthetic strokes. Include cached text,
uncached text, camera movement, stale hit-testing and reduced-motion presentation.

Measure acknowledgement, first prefix, unchanged-prefix intervals, question age,
final catch-up after input stops, cancellation, page input delay and memory. Collect
visible frames/transitions alongside spans; FPS alone does not show staleness.

Prediction: progressive output plus marked replacement is intelligible; shared
slowdown is noticeable but honest; no sped-up wait burst follows construction.
Ask viewers whether the system heard the question and which answer is current,
without telling them which treatment is preferred. Keep actual user observation
separate from automated latency proxies. Falsifier: feedback is read as completion,
stale status is missed, valid prefixes are confusing, or independent companions
make shared slowdown unacceptable. Such evidence reopens the relevant ruling,
not D011 and not all choices at once.

** P7 — Schedule-invariance and lifecycle adversary
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-p7
:END:

Fixed questions at small/large capacities and budgets; smooth/janky opportunities;
identity synchronous admission and controlled delayed replies; dependency reads
and mutual cycles; reset/new play/edit and repeated mount/dispose. Compare canonical
logical event traces, accepted transforms, errors and terminal geometry. For endless
programs compare the same logical prefix, not equal wall time or endless completion.
Normalize transport path batching before comparing geometry: a hash of ring-buffer
record boundaries is not automatically a geometry oracle.

Prediction: all treatments preserve fixed-input meaning; only reveal changes.
Falsifier: any divergent sibling read, lost ink, late stale mutation, admission/law
bypass, or unbounded resource residue. Run the existing determinism, backpressure,
residency, readout/figure, lifecycle and timeline witnesses as the regression floor.

* Design of trials and evidence ledger
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-trials
:LENS: empiricist
:END:

1. Pin the source actually executed. HEAD is insufficient in a dirty checkout.
   Record relevant source hashes, dependency/runtime versions, fixture, input trace,
   configuration, instrumentation and output digest. Never clean away unrelated work.
2. Run deterministic falsifiers first. A causal or lifetime failure rejects the
   treatment regardless of speed. Hard invariants use exact comparisons, not p-values.
3. Pilot the instrument: verify overhead, time units, stable controls and worst
   indivisible spans. Then record device-specific experience targets before comparing
   treatments. No universal 4 ms or 60 Hz claim is a target by default.
4. Change one mechanism per first comparison. Fixed budget while testing H; fixed H
   while testing grouping; fixed grouping while testing controller. Then cross the
   surviving factors to expose interactions. A giant combined before/after proves little.
5. Separate cold startup from steady state. Use at least five independent cold runs
   per browser treatment and twenty balanced paired warm trials after a declared
   warmup. Randomize AB/BA order with a recorded seed; run performance trials alone.
   These are starting sample plans, not proof of statistical power. Extend if variability
   makes the interval too wide for the proposed decision.
6. Pair runs on the same device/load and identical input trace. Report sample counts,
   p50/p95/max, paired differences and uncertainty across independent trials; frames
   within one run are not independent replications. Count censored/nonsettling cases.
7. Run small factorial blocks after a cause is established: workload × capacity ×
   opportunity cadence × input pattern. Include a same-question negative control,
   positive overload control, and a semantic-read adversary. Reduce by justified
   representative cases rather than silently dropping expensive cells.
8. Archive raw JSONL, environment manifest, visible transitions and summaries. Retain
   every failed seed and smallest reproducer. Do not select only the best warm run.
9. Rank surviving candidates by responsiveness, useful-answer age, prefix coherency,
   retained memory and complexity. No unexplained weighted "performance score".
   A speed gain whose control also moved is unresolved attribution, not a win.
10. Record each conclusion as: question; prior prediction; observed result; alternative
    explanation; ruling/reopen condition; surviving test; instrument exit. Timing
    measurements remain evidence, while stable counterexamples become regression tests.

Current instrument and result seat: [[file:../../probe/live-rendering/README.org][probe/live-rendering]].
Record /not run/, /inconclusive/, /censored/, /supports/, or /falsifies/ explicitly.
A successful baseline is not support for an unimplemented treatment.

* Smallest sequence of intervention and stopping rules
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: live-rendering-sequence
:LENS: pragmatist empiricist
:END:

- Stage 0: P0 diagnostics and existing tests; reconcile stale module claims.
- Stage 1: P1 classifier/H spike, isolated; prove healthy waits and no debt.
- Stage 2: P2/P3 display boundaries and ownership, with P4 accounting. Their
  implementation order follows observed dependencies; no giant collector assumed.
- Stage 3: P7 regression/determinism before browser tuning.
- Stage 4: P5 spans/controller experiments and P6 viewer/ensemble measurements.
- Stage 5: fold earned findings into this contract, promote falsifiers into tests,
  and either adopt the smallest treatment or keep current behavior with reasons.

Stop a treatment immediately for semantic divergence, stale lifetime mutation,
unsafe interaction, output loss or an unbounded staging path. Stop and diagnose an
ambiguous gate before implementing a heuristic clock. An unbroken expensive call
is evidence to split or optimize that call, not evidence for another opportunity
source. A shared-clock failure reopens clock scope only after confirming its cause.

Do not implement replay, idle computation beyond H, a worker, per-figure scheduling,
a new ownership store or a new dependency graph as an unmeasured rescue. A need may
be earned later. Favor deleting false assumptions over enlarging the system.
